messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran into a weird behavior in prod: requests that omit X-Client-Version and X-Api-Version are getting rejected by the v2 router for tenants that previously fell back to v1. Not returning a soft-fallback; just 403.

maria: ugh. is that the new strict-handshake check from the header-refactor?

alex: I think so. The router binary added a check to require version metadata for v2 routing because of affinity issues. But we never intended to hard-block headerless clients for tenants that are pinned to v1.

jamal: Can you paste an example request/response?

alex: request snippet: `POST /v2/generate` with no X-Api-Version or X-Client-Version. Response: 403 {"error":"version header required"}. Happened during a controlled traffic spike; several SDK customers reported failures.

olivia: Oof. Customers on older SDKs that rely on implicit v1 behavior will break. We need a short rollback or a soft-fallback knob.

maria: We ship a console affordance for 'legacy headerless compatibility' in past experiments. Should we flip that on as a global emergency flag? @jamal do we have a backend toggle?

jamal: There is a config flag but it's scoped to route groups and defaults to OFF. I can flip it per-tenant but doing it globally could mask the handshake bug.

alex: Proposal: add a temporary soft-mode where the router logs a warning and emits a metric, but still routes headerless requests to pinned v1 variants when available. Call metric route.accept.headerless.*. Avoid global silent accept. We'll need console visibility + per-tenant override.

maria: Agreed. Important: quota/accounting. If the router silently routes headerless -> v1, billing needs to attribute tokens correctly and the console should reflect model variant used. Otherwise customer sees weird bill/latency mismatch.

olivia: On the console side we can add a small banner in tenant details: "Some requests suppressed version headers; routing to v1 fallback" and a link to the opt-out toggle. Also surface the new metric in the per-route dashboard.

jamal: Implementation sketch: router accepts option `legacy_header_handling = { mode: "soft", emit_metric: true }`. Pseudoconfig:```json
{
  "legacy_header_handling": {
    "mode": "soft", 
    "emit_metric": true,
    "per_tenant_overrides": true
  }
}
```

maria: Nice. Metric names: `router.request.headerless.count`, `router.request.headerless.routed_to_v1.count`, and `router.request.headerless.rejected.count`. Make them taggable by tenant_id + route.

alex: Also important: trace annotation so we can search traces where headerless=true. Add tag `headerless=true` on the span.

jamal: I can do the router patch. Two follow-ups: 1) a console toggle UI and 2) an infra flag to enable per-tenant overrides in config store. Which should be owned by who?

olivia: I can wire the UI banner + toggle; will need an API endpoint to set tenant override (admin only).

maria: I'll own telemetry/dashboard changes (metrics + per-route panels). Also add an alert if `router.request.headerless.rejected.count` spikes — we should detect regressions.

alex: Operational play: jamal flips default to `soft` in a canary region first (us-west-2), monitor metrics for 1 hour, then roll global if stable. We'll keep verbose logs for 24h, then rotate to warning-only.

jamal: ok I’ll push a small patch today (+ unit tests). Plan to deploy a canary Friday AM.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: router-service v3.14.2-canary queued — owner=jamal — will run in us-west-2.

olivia: For the console, can we display the last 7 days of headerless metrics inline under tenant -> traffic insights? helps customer-support answer tickets.

maria: yes, adding a small sparkline and the 3 metric counters should be doable in the next sprint.

alex: Legal/Compliance note: make sure we don't change data residency semantics when routing to different variants. Jamal pls confirm routing respects tenant region constraints.

jamal: confirmed — routing respects region affinity; the change only affects header validation and fallback logic.

maria: Quick QA checklist before canary: 1) metric emitted with tenant+route tags, 2) trace annotation present, 3) token billing attribution preserved, 4) console toggle API responds, 5) per-tenant override honored.

jamal: copying checklist to PR. tagging: @olivia for console API contract.

olivia: got it. I'll prepare a tiny admin endpoint: PATCH /tenants/{id}/settings { "legacy_header_handling": "allow" } and wire UI.

alex: Thanks team. After canary, let's run a small synthetic test suite hitting headerless requests from old SDKs and ensure behavior matches v1. Also create a short customer-facing note for support.

maria: I'll draft the support note and the alert runbook (what to do if rejections spike).

jamal: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pulls/2934 (WIP) — will update with canary manifests.

alex: :thumbsup: keep the thread posted.
